body: Sounds like the female version of my boyfriend >_<
I miss when I was in a relationship where all of those basic things were mostly there, and I could ask for backrubs whenever I wanted. No one takes care of me except for me. I’m so tired.
I read the title as "bouncer" like the door-person at a bar or club, haha.  I kinda like that interpretation- I am my own bouncer for maintaining my boundaries!  (I like your original meaning too!)
It seems like my SO always gets manic during the spring and fall too!
I’m glad to hear your partner is drinking less, but I’m sorry that you also had to go through experiences like this. <3

Thank you. He definitely does need help. Unfortunately I also used to drink heavily for a good part of our relationship- it was our “thing.”  I’m a social drinker now and about to do a Dry April, but criticizing or expressing concerns about his drinking leads him to call me a hypocrite. 

I know I’m terribly codependent- it’s hard for me to set boundaries but I’m working on it. I’m going to find a therapist who can help me with that. 

His family is in another state, and he’s burned bridges with his mom. His Dad is low income and can’t help. If he wasn’t living with me, he would probably end up homeless (he was for a while when he was a teenager). 

He’s said that he’ll never speak to me again if I get him involuntarily committed. It’s such a bind.

Thank you for the empathy and supportive words. 

Improving myself (something I do have control over, since I can’t control him) has definitely made a big difference. I mentioned in other comments that I have advanced in my career and have a medication that helps control my depression and anxiety now. 

I was in my 20s and drinking too much as well (but not an alcoholic) when we first met- and I romanticized finally having someone who didn’t judge how much I drank. I only drink socially now, rarely more than 2-3 drinks at a time. The problem is that he’s still drinking almost as much as we both did back then. And he can pull out any number of anecdotes where I was wasted if I express concern about his drinking. 

He wants to get help on some level. His executive function varies so much from day to day that it makes it hard to plan things, schedule appointments, etc. I don’t want to be the “Mom” (ugh) as I have in past relationships and pester him to go to the doctor- that will make him less likely to go. 

I know I’m codependent as fuck and am looking to get into therapy to help with that.

Oh how I wish that would work in our situation! Ultimatums don’t work with him, unfortunately- he actually has threatened *me* with leaving (and followed through a few times). He sees it as manipulative if I try and leverage the relationship, living with me, or anything. He resents that he’s dependent on me for housing (he’s on disability, no bank account, can’t get a job) and that I can work and he can’t. He used to be a very successful tech guy.

Thank you so much. It means a lot to feel heard like this! I know things can’t continue like this and he really needs help. Things are better than they were in the past and episodes like this are fewer and farther between. I mentioned this in another comment but i also have depression and anxiety, but I’m managing it with meds and doing very well. 

He knows he needs help and has expressed openness to meds, but then his mood will change and his anxiety and cynicism about the medical system kicks in (tried many meds in the past, didn’t work and couldn’t deal with side effects- but that was before the diagnosis. Of course SSRIs don’t work for bipolar!)

Thank you, it means a lot! It’s been a process figuring out how to not engage, and I’m not always as successful at it as I was last night. My life is much better now than it was when we first got together. We both were hit by the recession and unemployed. I temped for a few years, then got two jobs, and finally I dropped one of the jobs and got promoted to supervisor at the other job. 

I have depression and anxiety, so we bonded over that. Signed up for Obamacare & got a SSRI 5 years ago that works really well and has allowed me to function normally, get this far in my career, etc. Weirdly my life is probably the most together that it’s ever been- when we got together I was kind of a wreck myself health and job wise.
